register.name: pr_auc_simulator
register.source: outputs/source_comparison.json — 150 held-out simulations, 15,911 aligned rows, horizon 3 (6 months)
register.note: Screen skill when the fields come from the simulator itself. The ceiling our own surrogate is measured against.

register.name: pr_auc_surrogate
register.note: Screen skill in the configuration we would actually deploy. 99.0% retention of the simulator's skill.

register.name: pr_auc_persistence
register.note: 'Assume next period looks like this one.' The honest floor for a 6-month horizon, which sits at a different phase of the storage cycle. At horizons that are whole cycles this rises above 0.99 and the task stops being forecasting at all.

register.name: positive_rate
register.note: Base rate of elevated-leakage rows under our own T3 label at the 90th-percentile flux threshold. NOT a real-world fault base rate — it is a property of where we drew the threshold.

register.name: assessment_latency_s
register.source: Timed against the deployed API, 2026-08-14: POST /v1/assessments, simulation 0, timestep 31, 20 sampled faults, warm instance
register.note: Wall clock including network, on a Render free tier at 0.1 CPU. A pessimistic basis for a unit cost, which is the useful direction.

register.name: hypotheses_per_field_prediction
register.source: docs/PRESENTATION_CONTEXT.md — 1,000 realisations x 20 fault draws per realisation
register.note: The coverage the decoupling buys: the fault is not an input to the U-Net, so one field prediction is re-scored against every fault hypothesis without re-running the field.

register.name: prior_bad_fault
register.source: No published base rate exists for conductive faults at candidate storage sites. Swept across the full plausible span.
register.note: The prior that a site harbours a fault conductive enough to matter. Swept because the VOI answer genuinely depends on it — a screen is worth nothing at a site nobody doubted and nothing at a site nobody would approve.

register.name: hypotheses_simulated_unaided
register.source: Inferred from simulator runtime: a full-physics run is multi-hour, so a screening campaign affords a handful of scenarios.
register.note: The number of fault scenarios an operator can afford to simulate without us. This is the quantity our coverage is compared against, so the comparison is stated as a range, not a strawman of one.

register.name: mitigation_to_loss_ratio
register.source: NO SOURCE OPENED. Would require a workover/appraisal cost and a containment-failure cost, neither of which we have a citation for.
register.note: The only economic parameter the headline result depends on, and it enters as a ratio, so both unknown costs cancel to one unknown number — which we then sweep over three decades rather than pick.

register.note: Not consumed by the headline result. Listed so the register is complete and so the omission is visible rather than quiet.
